clue.text: Put off the route to Hampshire town

parts.note: ST is short for street, a route through a town
Andover is a market town in Hampshire, a county in southern England

explanation.surface: Directions for the road that leads to a town in Hampshire.
explanation.walkthrough: ANDOVER is a town in Hampshire, a county on England's south coast; 'to' simply joins the street to it.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand something over is to postpone it, leaving it to be dealt with later.

clue.text: To stow away in a ship, soldiers start to hide

indicators.note: in tells us the soldiers are placed within the letters for the ship

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve soldiers

indicators.note: the start to a word is its opening letter, here the first letter of hide

explanation.surface: A stowaway's instructions: soldiers boarding a vessel begin to conceal themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to hide' gives only the opening letter; the Territorial Army is Britain's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To stash goods is to hide or store them away out of sight.

clue.text: Shot an office worker in the middle of the race

parts.note: an gives the letter A

indicators.note: the office worker is set in the middle of the letters standing for the race, splitting them

parts.note: the TT (Tourist Trophy) is the famous motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
a temp is a temporary office worker

explanation.surface: Someone fires at a clerk in the thick of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like gunfire, but it means a try, as in 'have a shot'. The TT is the Isle of Man motorbike race.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot at something is an attempt, a go or try.

clue.text: Soldier restarted in a new organization

indicators.note: putting the letters of restarted into a new organization means rearranging them

explanation.surface: A soldier begins again in a fresh unit.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram is signalled by 'in a new organization'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Desert Rats were the British 7th Armoured Division in North Africa in the Second World War, and a member is so called.

clue.text: Justification of the victory sign

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for victory, as in the V-sign
an indication is a sign or signal

explanation.surface: Explaining what the V-for-victory gesture means.
explanation.definitionFit: Vindication is proof that a claim or action was right, a justification of it.

clue.text: Listened to music of the bird

indicators.note: listened to tells us to hear the word for the music rather than read it

parts.note: rock is a style of popular music

explanation.surface: Someone tuned in to the song of a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'music' is ROCK, which sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The roc is a giant mythical bird from Arabian legend, as in the Sinbad tales.

clue.text: Net that's transparent

explanation.surface: A mesh that you can see straight through.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear a sum is to net it as profit after costs; clear also means see-through, like glass.

clue.text: To confine murderer inside is hard

indicators.note: inside says the letter for hard sits within the murderer's name

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis, the first murderer
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Locking up a killer from within is difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: Cain, the Bible's first murderer, takes H (hard) inside him; 'is' just joins the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: To chain a prisoner is to fetter him, keeping him confined.

clue.text: City upset about a ruler

indicators.note: about says the backwards city wraps round the other piece
in a down clue upset turns the city's name upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: Rome is the Eternal City
per means a, as in 'ten pounds a head'

explanation.surface: A city overthrown around its sovereign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' suits a down clue, turning the city so it reads EMOR; 'about' then wraps it round the word meaning 'a', as in so much per head.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is a supreme sovereign ruling an empire.

clue.text: You'll bear unfurled colour

indicators.note: a flag unfurled is opened out, and these letters are spread and reset in a new order

explanation.surface: You will carry a flag spread open to the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfurled' signals the anagram of YOULLBEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal blue is a deep, bright shade of blue.

clue.text: Craftsman biased 'after being robbed of a little money

indicators.note: being robbed of something means losing it, so the coin's letter is taken away from the word for biased

parts.note: a partisan view is biased, one-sided
P is a penny, a small coin

explanation.surface: A tradesman turns prejudiced once someone has stolen his small change.
explanation.walkthrough: PARTISAN loses P (penny), the 'little money'.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a skilled manual worker, a maker of goods by hand.

clue.text: Cautious about river bed

indicators.note: about says the word for cautious goes round the river

parts.note: chary means wary or cautious
the Po is the longest river in Italy

explanation.surface: Someone is wary of the bed of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'river bed' reads as one phrase, but 'river' is the Po and 'bed' alone is the definition. A charpoy is a light Indian bedstead.
explanation.definitionFit: A charpoy is a light Indian bedstead of woven tape or rope on a wooden frame.

clue.text: Poet had a good run in America

definitions.text: had a good run in America

explanation.surface: A poet enjoyed a successful spell in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: In baseball, to hit a home run is to homer, the American sense the second half points to.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer is the Greek poet of the Iliad and Odyssey; in US baseball, to homer is to hit a home run.

clue.text: Popular military man, for the most part

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
a general is a senior army officer

explanation.surface: A well-liked army officer, by and large.
explanation.definitionFit: In general means usually or mostly, on the whole.

clue.text: Wealth comprising foreign money given to staff by Gladstone

indicators.note: comprising says the word for wealth holds the currency inside it

parts.note: gold stands for wealth or riches
the rand is the currency of South Africa
to man a post is to staff it

explanation.surface: Riches, including foreign currency, handed to employees by the Victorian prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gladstone' looks like a bag or a man giving money, but it is the definition: the Victorian prime minister William Gladstone was nicknamed the Grand Old Man.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian Liberal prime minister William Gladstone was popularly called the Grand Old Man, or GOM.

clue.text: Strike back, and strike at the right time

indicators.note: back says the word for strike is read from its last letter to its first

parts.note: to tap is to strike lightly

explanation.surface: Hit back, and hit at just the right moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TAP round; the answer also means to strike gently and, as an adverb, timely.
explanation.definitionFit: To pat is to hit lightly with the hand; pat as an adverb means opportunely, aptly timed.

clue.text: Sizzling music with exciting rhythms

parts.note: piping is the music of pipes, such as bagpipes
hot jazz is music with fast, exciting rhythms

explanation.surface: Lively music with thrilling beats.
explanation.definitionFit: Piping hot food is very hot, so hot it sizzles.

clue.text: One right into real drama at sea

definitions.text: One right into real drama at sea

indicators.note: into says the letters for one and right go inside the rearranged words
at sea means confused, so the words real and drama are jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A man caught up in genuine excitement on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' shuffles the two words into REARADMAL, and 'into' inserts one and right. The whole clue doubles as a picture of a naval officer afloat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rear admiral is a naval flag officer, someone whose career is spent on warships.

clue.text: Ship is allowed on the river

parts.note: may means is permitted, as in 'you may go'
a river is a flower in crossword language, something that flows

explanation.surface: A vessel has permission to sail on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'river' is FLOWER in the sense of a thing that flows, not a bloom. The Mayflower carried the Pilgrim Fathers to America in 1620.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mayflower was the ship that took the Pilgrim Fathers to New England in 1620.

clue.text: Don't exaggerate trouble in t'mill — tidy up

indicators.note: trouble signals that the letters are stirred up and disordered

explanation.surface: A northern mill worker, told to tidy up, is asked not to overstate the difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' shuffles TMILLTIDYUP; 't'mill' is northern English dialect for 'the mill'.
explanation.definitionFit: To put it mildly is to understate, the opposite of overstating something.

clue.text: Insect was first diverted

parts.note: a tick is a small blood-sucking creature, loosely called an insect
to have led is to have been in front, first

explanation.surface: A bug that came first was sent another way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diverted' looks like turned aside, but here it means amused.
explanation.definitionFit: Tickled means amused or entertained, and diverted has that same sense.

clue.text: Institute legal proceedings against girl

explanation.surface: Taking a young woman to court.
explanation.definitionFit: To sue is to bring a lawsuit; Sue is a girl's name, short for Susan.

clue.text: Majestic vessel, a British ship, but not the last in the navy

parts.note: sub is short for submarine, a vessel

indicators.note: but not tells us to drop the following letter from the slang word

parts.note: limey is old American slang for a British sailor or ship

indicators.note: the last in a word is its final letter, here of navy

explanation.surface: A grand boat, a British warship that is not the last in the fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not' drops the final letter of 'navy' from the slang term; Chambers gives limey as a British sailor or ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Sublime means awe-inspiringly grand or noble, as majestic does.

clue.text: In no state to go round at night

indicators.note: In at the start says the turning goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: Cal is short for California, a US state
to turn is to go round, rotate

explanation.surface: Too unwell to make a round trip after dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In no state' reads as an idiom, but NO and CAL (California) hold TURN.
explanation.definitionFit: Nocturnal means happening or active during the night.

clue.text: Range of size, and of colour also

indicators.note: of points to letters taken from within the words colour also

explanation.surface: A selection of dimensions, and of shades too.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside 'colour also'; 'Range' here is a mountain chain, and a large one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Urals are a major mountain chain dividing Europe from Asia.

clue.text: Trouble brought about by invading country

indicators.note: invading says the word by forces its way inside
a ship brought about turns round, so the word for trouble is reversed

parts.note: to ail is to trouble, as in 'what ails you?'

explanation.surface: Unrest stirred up by an invasion of a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought about' is a sailing term for turning round, giving LIA; 'invading' puts the little word inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Libya is a North African nation on the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Bill goes to hospital with another man hurt

parts.note: AC stands for account, a bill
H is the map abbreviation for hospital
Ed is a man's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: Bill is taken to hospital along with a second injured man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name, which 'another man' encourages, but it is AC, an account.
explanation.definitionFit: Ached means felt pain, was sore.

clue.text: Man taken 'to court — it's for lifting canvas

parts.note: Hal is a man's name, short for Henry
a yard is a courtyard, an enclosed court

explanation.surface: A man is hauled before a judge, all about raising a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canvas' suggests painting, but here it means sails.
explanation.definitionFit: A halyard is a rope used to hoist a sail or flag on a ship.

clue.text: Pickpocket, one apprehended by a refugee

indicators.note: apprehended by means caught and held, so the refugee's letters enclose the one

parts.note: DP stands for displaced person, a refugee
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A thief is caught by someone fleeing persecution.
explanation.walkthrough: DP (displaced person) holds I (one).
explanation.definitionFit: Dip is slang for a pickpocket, who dips into others' pockets.

clue.text: Freeing hawks — I'm stupidly sentimental

indicators.note: freeing the letters lets them fly loose and land in a new order

explanation.surface: A falconer releasing birds admits to foolish emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Freeing' signals the anagram of HAWKSIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Mawkish means sickly or foolishly sentimental.

clue.text: The last shall be first, in, i.e, the Times

indicators.note: the biblical saying tells us to move the final letter to the front

parts.note: i.e. stands for the Latin id est, that is

explanation.surface: A biblical saying quoted in this very newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Times' looks like the newspaper but means seasons or times, as in Eastertide. 'i.e.' expands to ID EST, whose final T moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Tide is an old word for a time or season, as in Yuletide.

clue.text: Prison day draws to a close for correspondent

parts.note: pen is US slang for a penitentiary, a prison
Fri is short for Friday
to end is to draw to a close

explanation.surface: A prisoner's day nears its end, for one who writes letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen-friend is someone you exchange letters with, usually without meeting.
